newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank rate cut not due to strong markka -PM.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank rate cut not due to strong markka -PM.

text.p: The Bank of Finland cut its tender rate this morning basing on the economic situation, not due to appreciation pressure on the markka, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Wednesday.
Asked after the economic council meeting to comment on whether the central bank had moved to weaken the markka, Lipponen told Reuters "surely not".
"Long interest rates have fallen briskly, all economic indicators are such that they strengthen confidence in the stability of the economy," he said.
"In my opinion, it was a good decision," he said.
"...the Bank of Finland lowers its tender rate only when there are objective economic prerequisites for it," he added.
The bank on Wednesday morning surprised financial markets with a 15 basis points cut in its key tender rate to 3.10 percent.
